changes: Created and audited the ProofStory acceptance-topology execution plan. It preserves milestone ledger and existing evidence ownership, defines verificationIntent-owned planned paths, independently derived per-adapter coverage bases, phase-separated PLAN and pre-REVIEW gates, global closure freshness, negative controls, rollout waves, and a human audit rubric.
usage: Use the execution plan as the approved source for creating separate Wave 1, 1A, 2, 2A, 3, 3A, and 4 implementation Stories; do not implement runtime gates inside B-4444 or create a writable acceptance matrix.
expectedOutcome: The user can inspect one approved plan that explains canonical ownership, forbids a parallel acceptance-matrix truth source, specifies structural and executable gates, and provides bounded implementation waves with mechanical audit criteria.
actualTranscript: The live-smoke command exited 0 and displayed the no-writable-matrix invariant, acceptance_topology_check, pre_review_check, Wave 1/1A sections, verification and mutation matrix, and human audit checklist from the committed document.
outcomeDiff: No material difference: the committed plan and captured transcript expose all expected user-visible planning outcomes. Runtime gate implementation remains intentionally deferred to separate Wave Stories.
limitations: This Story is documentation-only and intentionally does not implement the proposed schemas, commands, adapters, or lifecycle gates. Open decisions are explicitly bound to later Wave entry criteria.
pitfalls: Four REVIEW rounds found and fixed seven issues: PLAN new-path deadlock, per-adapter auditability, circular planned-path ownership, phase-basis example drift, file-ref mismatch, missing mutation bites, and PLAN actual-diff ambiguity. Future implementers must preserve verificationIntent ownership and PLAN/pre-REVIEW basis separation.
